newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan utilites prepare for nuclear waste return.
newsitem.headline: Japan utilites prepare for nuclear waste return.

text.p: Four Japanese utilities have asked Japan's science agency to check on the safety of canisters containing radioactive waste due to be transported to Japan from France next year, an agency official said on Friday.

Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO), Kansai Electric Power Co Inc, Shikoku Electric Power Co Inc and Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc are planning to jointly ship to Japan 40 canisters containing radioactive material that has been sealed in glass.
A Science and Technology Agency official said that government officials would be dispatched to France to check on the safety of the waste which is due to be shipped between January and March 1997.
Japan, which lacks its own facilities, relies on France and Britain to reprocess its nuclear fuel.
Spent Japanese uranium fuel is reprocessed into plutonium at a French plant, and the waste produced must be stored in Japan.
The first shipment took place in 1995 amid heavy protest.
Next year's shipment will be the second.
